paper1.title: Endogenous Contestability and Technological Scale: Entry, Selection, and the Value of Comparison

editorial_fit.assessment: Journal of Evolutionary Economics is the first fit because the article connects entry, historical selection, technological capability, and endogenous learning. Review of Industrial Organization is a plausible alternative for the strategic access game and conditional competition-policy test. This is a submission-oriented theory draft; suitability does not imply acceptance or established novelty.
editorial_fit.requirements: The Journal of Evolutionary Economics guidelines call for a 150–250-word abstract, 4–6 keywords, JEL classification, editable manuscript, author-date references, and relevant declarations. Native Word equations are appropriate. Substantive AI assistance is disclosed below. Corresponding-author contact, residence (no institutional affiliation), ORCID if available, funding, conflicts, and author-contribution metadata require the author's factual completion before submission.
editorial_fit.unpublished_foundation: The October 2026 Shadow Futures author manuscript is identified in the body, with its associated public record. It is excluded from the bibliography because the target publisher asks that unpublished work be mentioned in text rather than listed as accepted or published research. The public record's July 2026 revision must not be represented as identical to the local October manuscript.
editorial_fit.remaining_author_work: Confirm accountability for the model and proofs, supply submission metadata, and undertake a broader novelty search and field-specific editorial review. No empirical evidence or general-equilibrium claim is asserted.

paper4.title: Competition Policy for Informative Market Access

editorial_fit.rationale: The article addresses industrial organization and public policy through an implementable theory of remedies with testable evidence requirements. Its formal common-rule results and explicit hypothetical design fit the journal's interest in significant theory accessible to nonspecialists. The absence of field estimates remains an editorial limitation; fit is a reasoned targeting choice and not an acceptance prediction.
requirements: Abstract 150–250 words; four to six keywords.

Author contributions and competing-interest information supplied through the submission interface.
Generative LLM assistance documented in a suitable manuscript section; authorship remains human.

paper5.title: Taxing Lost Comparison: Decision Information, Private Testing, and Costed Corrective Instruments

editorial_fit.assessment: International Tax and Public Finance is the first target: its official scope includes theoretical research across public economics, and this article solves corrective instruments and public-expenditure choice. Economics of Governance is an alternative if evaluation provision, institutional enforceability, and appropriation are emphasized. Neither recommendation predicts acceptance or establishes novelty.
editorial_fit.requirements: Current ITPF guidelines require a 150–250-word abstract, 4–6 keywords, JEL codes, author-date citations, relevant declarations, and editable source. LaTeX is recommended; Word is accepted. A Word manuscript should retain native editable equations. Generative AI assistance is disclosed. Martin Erlic has no institutional affiliation. Correspondence details, residence where needed, ORCID if available, funding, conflicts, and author contributions remain factual submission metadata for the author to complete.
editorial_fit.unpublished_foundation: The supplied October 2026 Shadow Futures manuscript is identified in the body with the associated SSRN record, rather than represented as published or accepted in the bibliography. The public July revision is not asserted to match that local version.
editorial_fit.remaining_author_work: Confirm the theoretical assumptions and proof accountability; supply metadata; undertake broader novelty and sector-specific review. No real-sector tax rate, claim of actual undertaxation, or unconditional Pareto improvement is asserted.
